title: Al-Mudhill, the one who humbles
hookLine: the one who humbles, who takes away false honor
tomorrow: a woman argues, and a whole surah is named for her. why?

cards: A haul video. Bags lined up across a bed, a car key on a ring, and under it a wall of comments: goals. The Qur'an has a comment section like that.
Qarun steps out among his people in all his finery. His treasure is so large, the text says, that its keys alone would weigh down a band of strong men.
And the crowd that wants this life says it out loud: if only we had what Qarun has. Then the ground opens. Qarun and his house are gone.
The next morning, the people who said if only wake up, and…

teach.b: …they say something new. If Allah had not been gracious to us, they say, He would have swallowed us too. The ones who wanted his place now give thanks they never got it.
That turn is the work of today's Name: Al-Mudhill, the one who humbles. It sounds harsh, until you hear what Qarun had said when people warned him.

teach.h: IT CAME FROM WHAT I KNOW.
teach.b: I was given all this, he said, because of what I know. A gift he had started calling his own achievement, the way a borrowed jacket starts to feel like yours after a while.
Al-Mudhill takes away false honor, the kind you borrowed and forgot was borrowed.
In the Qur'an you meet it as a verb, inside a prayer in Surah Al Imran: "Thou exaltest whom Thou wilt and Thou abasest whom Thou wilt. In Thy hand is the good." Look at that last line.

teach.h: IN THY HAND IS THE GOOD.
teach.b: Raising and lowering, both in one hand, and that hand holds the good.

Qarun had the keys. He never had the hand. Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight: some scholars teach that this Name is best said together with yesterday's, Al-Mu'izz al-Mudhill, so nobody hears only half of it.
Status is weather. It rolls in, it moves on. The one who sends it does not.

how: Muslims learn the Names of Allah from the Qur'an and from the list in Jami' at-Tirmidhi and call on them in du'a; some scholars teach that a Name like al-Mudhill is said together with its pair, al-Mu'izz.

o: the one who humbles, taking back false honor
the one who keeps the proud rich forever
the one who punishes each mistake at once

games.q: who's who in the story — tap the pairs.
p: said his wealth came from what he knew
wished for his place, then gave thanks
raising and lowering in one hand

s: Al-Mudhill means God enjoys putting people down
in the prayer of 3:26, raising and lowering sit in one hand, and that hand holds the good.
in the Qur'an you meet this Name as a verb, inside a prayer
the crowd that envied Qarun kept wishing for his life afterward
the next morning they gave thanks that they never got it.

games.q: you won the award everyone wanted. at dinner your uncle says, 'all you, kid. you earned every bit.' which reply sits closest to today's Name?
o: 'thanks, i really did. nobody worked harder than me.'
'thanks. i worked for it, and it's still a gift, and it'll pass.'
'it was nothing, honestly. anyone could have won it.'
games.why: Qarun's slip wasn't having wealth; it was calling the gift his own doing. brushing it off misses too. thank people, and hold it lightly.

practice: Grab a pen and a scrap of paper. Write one title you'd love people to use for you: captain, top of the class, the one with all the answers. Read it once, fold it in half, and set it face down.
For the sit, rest your hands open on your knees, holding nothing.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mudhill. The one who humbles, who takes back honor that was only ever on loan.

orig.note: Arabic: the one who humbles. some scholars pair it with al-Mu'izz, the Giver of Honor.

carryVoice: Keep this: status passes, and the one who gives it and takes it back stays. See you tomorrow.

sources.q: Thou exaltest whom Thou wilt and Thou abasest whom Thou wilt. In Thy hand is the good.

sources.ref: Qur'an 28:76–82 (Qarun's treasure and keys, his claim, the crowd's wish, the earth swallowing him, the crowd's words the next morning)
Jami' at-Tirmidhi 3507 (the list of the Names, including al-Mu'izz and al-Mudhill)
